subject: SOC 2 coverage: inclusive day endpoints & evidence timestamps (need confirmation)
messages:
From: Melissa Tran <mtran@brightpath-auditors.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security <acme-security@acme.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — clarifying coverage endpoints and evidence timing

Hi Rohan,

Quick question as we prepare the fieldwork: for Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report covering 2027-01-01 through 2027-12-31, does Redwood consider the coverage period to include the entire end date (i.e., up to and including 2027-12-31 23:59:59)?

Specifically the auditor team needs to know:
- Is the "end date" inclusive?
- What timezone is used for evidence capture timestamps (UTC vs local)?
- For point-in-time evidence (config snapshots, backups, log extracts), are objects/files tagged with the exact capture timestamp?

If there are any partial-day rollovers or migrations during the period boundary, we'll need a short bridge letter describing the timing. I've attached a request matrix with the ask list.

Can you confirm by EOD tomorrow? Acme's security team is copied for visibility.

Thanks,
Melissa Tran
Senior Manager, BrightPath Auditors
attachments: request_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet of data items requested)
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Melissa Tran <mtran@brightpath-auditors.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — clarifying coverage endpoints and evidence timing

Hi Melissa — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details: 1) yes, our intent is for the end date to be inclusive; 2) we record timestamps in UTC; 3) point-in-time evidence includes explicit capture timestamps.

Details:
- Inclusive endpoints: our policy is to treat a reporting-day as inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC. We rely on UTC to avoid daylight-savings ambiguity.
- Evidence tagging: config exports, backups, and log extracts created by our pipelines include an ISO8601 timestamp in the filename and in object metadata. Example: gs://redwood-evidence/2027/12/31/config-export-2027-12-31T23:59:58Z.json
- Migration/rollover notes: during 2027 we had a scheduled key rotation on 2027-12-31 that ran 23:45–23:55 UTC; no logging pipeline downtime occurred — logs continued to be ingested. We can provide the ingestion timeline if helpful.

I've attached our evidence manifest (redwood_evidence_manifest.pdf) which maps requested items to storage locations and timestamps. Neha/Karthik — can you confirm the pipeline retention and whether we want to propose a formal bridge letter that spells out the key rotation window?

Cheers,
Rohan
Sr. Manager, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_evidence_manifest.pdf
From: Melissa Tran <mtran@brightpath-auditors.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security <acme-security@acme.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — clarifying coverage endpoints and evidence timing

Thanks Rohan — that's very helpful. A couple clarifying points from the auditor perspective:

- "Inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC" is what we typically request; auditors will accept that provided the timestamps on evidence are consistent and there is no data gap.
- For the key rotation window you mentioned (23:45–23:55 UTC) we would want a short explanation if any evidence items were captured during that window and whether any control state changed (e.g., rotated keys causing replay or re-ingestion). If there's no interruption, that's fine — just document it.
- Regarding file/object timestamps: we prefer evidence items with embedded timestamps (filename + metadata) and a manifest that lists the exact capture time. That makes sampling straightforward.

If you can provide a draft bridge letter that states: the coverage end date is inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC and documents the 2027-12-31 rotation timing and that no evidence loss occurred, we can accept that and proceed. Also, please confirm whether the files' timestamps are in ISO8601 Zulu format (e.g., 2027-12-31T23:59:58Z).

I'll hold on the formal fieldwork until we receive the manifest + bridge letter.

Best,
Melissa
attachments: none
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Melissa Tran <mtran@brightpath-auditors.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-12T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — clarifying coverage endpoints and evidence timing

Hi Melissa,

Confirming the technical details from our side:

- Timestamps: All ingestion/backup/config exports include ISO8601 timestamps in UTC (Zulu). Filenames and object metadata both contain the timestamp; examples are included in the attached CSV manifest.
- Retention and sampling: Logs are retained for 13 months in GCS (project: redwood-logs-prod) with lifecycle rules. Sampling extracts include both the object_timestamp and the ingestion_timestamp fields.
- Key rotation event: On 2027-12-31 at 23:45 UTC we performed a KMS key rotation for our token-store. The operation completed at 23:55 UTC. There was no pipeline restart, and all log entries for that window show continuous ingestion (we verified sequence numbers). We will include a one-paragraph bridge letter stating the rotation timing and confirming no evidence gap.

Next steps:
1) I will upload a CSV manifest (evidence_manifest_v2.csv) with object paths and timestamps.
2) Draft a bridge letter (bridge_letter_draft.docx) for you to review that states: coverage inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC, rotation window, and confirmation of continuous ingestion.
3) We'll also attach the full SOC 2 Type II report once Q3 approvals complete — ETA 2028-04-25.

Let me know if you need the manifest in a different format.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
attachments: evidence_manifest_v2.csv, bridge_letter_draft.docx
From: Melissa Tran <mtran@brightpath-auditors.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security <acme-security@acme.com>
Date: 2028-04-17T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — clarifying coverage endpoints and evidence timing

Neha / Rohan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the level of detail.

We reviewed the manifest and the draft bridge letter. The manifest format is great and timestamps look consistent (ISO8601 Z). The bridge letter language is acceptable for our auditors; one small edit request for clarity around the rotation: please add the KMS key id/version and confirm that historical objects remain decryptable with prior key versions.

If you can drop an updated bridge_letter_draft.docx with that line, we can sign off and schedule the fieldwork. Also a reminder that Acme's security team would like an electronic copy of the full SOC 2 Type II report as soon as it's available (you mentioned 2028-04-25).

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to the updated doc.

Best,
Melissa
BrightPath Auditors
attachments: none
